steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Roman entertainment served political purposes — panem et circenses (bread and circuses) kept the population content

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Gladiatorial games (munera) originated as funeral rites and evolved into mass entertainment

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre) could hold 50,000-80,000 spectators and hosted gladiatorial combat and animal hunts

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Gladiators were usually slaves, prisoners of war or condemned criminals — though some volunteered for fame and money

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always discuss both the entertainment value AND the political function of Roman games The concept of panem et circenses is essential — it explains why entertainment mattered politically Use specific examples: the Colosseum, the Circus Maximus, gladiator types Consider the moral dimension — some Romans criticised the games as brutal and corrupting Link entertainment to social control, imperial propaganda and Roman identity
